signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.419, holding above its SMA20 while sitting below its SMA50. The G10 scorecard shows USD leading with a 1W average of +1.211% across 9 pairs, while NOK lags as the weakest G10 currency with a 1W average of -0.976% across 2 pairs, producing a wide bilateral spread of 2.188%. A SOFR 3.62% versus NOK policy rate 4.25% spread creates a NOK carry advantage, yet NOK underperforms severely under the weight of negative domestic growth momentum and broad dollar demand. The options and positioning data reflect strong divergence as USD/SEK retail short extremes highlight aggressive positioning against the dollar, matching the broader G10 momentum divergence. Trade bias: Long USD/NOK, structural dollar outperformance against lagging Scandies. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 24 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Norwegian employment data surprises further to the upside and compresses the G10 performance gap.

signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Outperformance + CB Policy Shift
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.703, positioned below its SMA20 at 156.89 and SMA50 at 159.14 following the Bank of Japan's rate hike to 1.25%. The 25d risk reversal sits at -2.08, showing strong put skew and elevated hedging demand for downside protection as the options market prices policy normalization. A SOFR 3.62% versus TONA 0.98% OIS differential provides supporting the dollar, even as the BoJ maintains an accommodative forward stance by signaling continued monetary support. Speculative positioning shows JPY net short at -53,255 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 30, reflecting an unwinding of historical shorts. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, policy normalization pressures the carry trade against entrenched yield differentials. Catalyst: BoJ Press Conference at 06:30 UTC. Risk: BoJ rhetoric turns hawkish enough to accelerate the unwind of speculative JPY shorts and break the 155 support level.

signals.title: GBP/JPY — Fair Value Dislocation + Carry Premium
signals.text: GBP/JPY trades at 209.412, reflecting strong cross-asset momentum as the pound maintains a carry advantage over the yen. The BEER fair value model places spot at a z-score of -3.02, indicating the pair is significantly cheap relative to model fair value at 215.47 with a solid fit. A SONIA 3.73% versus TONA 0.98% OIS carry differential of +275bp provides sustained fundamental support for the cross despite the broader G10 weakness in sterling. Retail sentiment shows an 81% long extreme in GBP/JPY, creating a contrarian caution flag as speculative positioning diverges from the fundamental valuation gap. Trade bias: Long GBP/JPY, mean-reversion toward fair value supported by a substantial carry premium. Catalyst: UK Retail Sales data at 06:00 UTC. Risk: Broad risk-off sentiment triggers a sharp liquidation of high-beta carry longs and accelerates spot divergence from fair value.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Options Skew
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1484, holding below its SMA20 at 1.1606 and SMA50 at 1.1539. Speculative positioning shows EUR net short at -46,381 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 34, while the 25d risk reversal rests near neutral at -0.22, signaling minimal directional options bias. A SOFR 3.62% versus ESTR 2.44% OIS differential provides favoring the dollar, reinforced by a real rate differential where the US sits at +1.59% against the euro area at +0.30%. Implied volatility sits at 4.7% against an HV30 of 4.3%, producing a mild vol premium of +0.4% that indicates subdued market fear ahead of European data releases. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, restrictive US rate stance and steady dollar outperformance capping upside momentum. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde Speech at 10:30 UTC. Risk: European inflation data prints significantly above expectations, forcing a hawkish repricing of ECB rate expectations.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Valuation Dislocation + Low Volatility
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8247, positioned above its SMA20 at 0.8107 and SMA50 at 0.8105. The BEER model flags the pair as rich with a z-score of +1.95, as spot at 0.8247 trades above model fair value at 0.8158. Options pricing shows implied volatility at 6.2% against an HV30 of 7.3%, yielding a negative VRP of -1.1% that highlights options complacency and thin protection demand. A SOFR 3.62% versus SARON -0.04% OIS differential delivers a +400bp carry advantage supporting long dollar positions, while retail sentiment shows a 69% short bias. Trade bias: Long USD/CHF, carry support offset by stretched valuation metrics and low implied volatility. Catalyst: SNB policy meeting 24 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Sudden risk-off repatriation flows drive a sharp safe-haven bid into the franc, unwinding the fair value premium.
